messages:
ashley (support): FYI - customer CS-3328 on hosted us-west-2 reporting a spike of 503/500 gateway responses starting ~09:12 PDT. seen across multiple routes. example request id: req_9a3f. customer on the line now, marking P1.
ashley (support): quick logs from proxy show upstream returned 502/503 and then container restart events: `upstream-runner exited with signal 11` and `container restartCount=3`. attaching clipped logs below.
ashley (support): ```
runner-7f8c stderr: fatal signal 11 (SIGSEGV), code=1, fault addr=0x7f2b7c000
runtime: attn_kernel.cu+0x42f  _ZN6attn::forward(...)
cuda: driver api error 77 (page fault on device)
dmesg: NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 79, pid=1123, GPU has fallen off the bus
```
miguel (eng-runtime): :eyes: do we know which model / batch size / seq len? any recent deploy to runtime?
ashley (support): customer payloads are single-turn chat, seq len ~512 avg, batch size 1 per request. model pinned to `open-redwood/reasoner-3b` on hosted. They call embedding+generate combo but failures are at generate.
sam (oncall): checking deploy history... there was a runtime release 08:50 with a KV prefetch optimization (kv-prefetch v2) rolled to 30% canary in us-west-2. linking deploy job: https://deploys.company.local/job/5234
jen (eng-ml): kv prefetch changed memory preallocation for large seqs, could increase GPU resident pages. possible memory corruption if pointer alignment changed after quantized kernel swap.
miguel (eng-runtime): pull coredump / stacktrace from runner-7f8c. sam can you grab `gcore` or coredump? also which driver/cuda on the node?
sam (oncall): node info: driver NVIDIA 525.89.02, CUDA 11.8. Host kernel 5.15. Running image: redwood/infer-runner:2026.03.09-rc. I pulled `/var/log/containers/runner-7f8c.log` - sending to thread.
sam (oncall): ```
[2026-03-15T09:11:58Z] runner-7f8c: calling prefetch_kv(range=0-128) -> allocated 1.2GB gpu mem
[2026-03-15T09:12:01Z] runner-7f8c: attn_kernel launch (seq=512, bs=1) -> kernel returned cudaErrorInvalidDevicePointer
[2026-03-15T09:12:01Z] kernel: NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 79: GPU page fault: context 0x...
[2026-03-15T09:12:02Z] crt: container runtime killed process with signal 11
```
miguel (eng-runtime): looks like page-faults at kernel launch immediately after the prefetch path. can we repro locally with a small harness? jen will try reproduce with latest model and kv prefetch toggled.
jen (eng-ml): spinning a repro - locally I can trigger a segfault-ish kernel failure if I enable prefetch + quantized int8 path on 512 seq for `reasoner-3b`. stepping through, the crash occurs inside attn gather kernel at address alignment boundary. suspect unsafe pointer arithmetic in prefetch slice mapping after the quantization switch.
ashley (support): customer asking for ETA, they're seeing timeouts in production. can we hotfix / rollback?
miguel (eng-runtime): recommended immediate mitigations: 1) disable kv-prefetch for hosted canary (kill the 08:50 release or set PREFETCH_ENABLE=false globally in affected pool) 2) revert quantized kernel flag 3) add per-run fallback to CPU decode for failing requests. which is fastest?
sam (oncall): I can flip PREFETCH_ENABLE=false for the canary pool now and scale new runners. applying change to us-west-2 canary pool. deploy-bot: request acknowledged.
deploy-bot: PREFETCH_ENABLE=false applied to runtime-canary-us-west-2 (job 5234-rollback). Instances draining and new pods launching. :shipit:
ashley (support): telling customer we have a mitigation rolling and to expect recovery in ~5-8 minutes.
sam (oncall): monitoring: error rate on the affected route dropped from 18% -> 2% within 6 minutes of the config flip. container restarts ceased on canary hosts.
miguel (eng-runtime): good. assign full rollback if CI + canary verification passes. also need to collect coredumps for postmortem. jen, can you get a reduced repro to run under memory sanitizer?
jen (eng-ml): yes. I have a minimal harness that reproduces in ~30s. sharing gist: https://internal.gists/repro/1902. Explanation: prefetch mapped unaligned slice for KV buffer when quantized kernel was chosen; subsequent attn kernel assumed 64B alignment -> device page fault on certain card/driver combos.
miguel (eng-runtime): note driver combo matters. older 525.x vs 530.x may differ in page fault tolerance. we should add a defensive check in prefetch to force aligned allocation and add a guard for device pointer validity before launch.
ashley (support): customer confirmed lowered errors and is running smoke tests. they asked for a timeline for full fix.
sam (oncall): recommend roll back kv-prefetch v2 from 30% -> 0% across region until fix is shipped. initiating region-wide rollback (job 5234-full-rollback). deploy-bot: rollback started.
deploy-bot: rollback complete for us-west-2. PREFETCH_ENABLE=false set across hosted pool.
miguel (eng-runtime): creating a ticket: INF-4612 to track root cause & code fix (pointer alignment + guard + better unit tests). proposed immediate actions: (a) patch prefetch to use cudaMallocAligned or pad allocations (b) add integ test for seq=512+quantized kernels on 525/530 drivers (c) add runtime feature flag for safe kernel path.
jen (eng-ml): I'll open a PR with the aligned allocation and unit tests. marking as high priority.
ashley (support): customer updated: "Thanks — errors stopped, we'll continue testing. pls CC us once permanent fix is out."
miguel (eng-runtime): ok assigning postmortem lead to eng-runtime + eng-ml. we'll publish incident notes and follow-up items after coredump analysis.
ashley (support): closing loop with customer and moving to status: monitoring. I'll update the ticket and add notes for billing/rate-limits if they ask for credits.
sam (oncall): adding note: mitigation had <5m impact window for canary region, full rollback took ~18m total. no data loss.
miguel (eng-runtime): thanks team. follow-ups: run cross-driver regression tests, add sentinel to detect device page-fault spike, and add an automated rollback if container restart rate > X%.
ashley (support): tagging docs: https://internal.runbooks/hosted/worker-pagefaults for follow-up edits. :white_check_mark:
